Learning Resources Recordable Answer Buzzers - Set of 4, Ages 3+ | Pre-K Personalized Sound Buzzers, Recordable Buttons, Game Show Buzzers, Perfect for Family Game and Trivia Nights I highly recommend these with one caveat. They aren't very loud so if you need to hear them from across a home they might not work for you.

I bought these for my 3 dogs, mostly for my geriatric Fox Terrier who asks for everything the same way -one scratch on the front door. And that scratch could mean he needs to go out into the back yard, or he wants me to open the front door so he can gaze out through the screen door, or his water is unacceptably dirty, or... You get the picture. I started with just one of the buttons and recorded my voice easily. The playback was clear, I really am impressed.

The problem is, our home is a bit older, about 130 years, it's not large but we have a closed floor plan with wonderfully thick walls. Unfortunately that means no matter how loud I shouted when recording you can't hear the playback if you aren't in the same room as the button. I guess my dog figured the front door is central enough that you can hear him scratch it from most areas in our home. Go figure.

Barbie Made to Move Doll, Orange Top Made to Move Teresa (blue top) can be posed almost like a real person. So it’s great for people who use her for photography, or in place of an artist wooden mannequin for drawing.

Her face and thick eyebrows seem to be modeled after 1980’s actress and model Brooke Shields. If you’re buying her for a child, the downside is the delicate and sparse hair plugs that will easily be yanked with any vigorous brushing like children tend to do.

The flash lightens up her skin tone in photos. In reality she has a very tanned orangey skin color. The deep orange tint is strange like a bad fake tan, but I got used to it.

I like the 2015 version of her face more than the 2019 version: she had softer eyes, two defined dimples, a more realistic natural-looking mouth, and less of an orange skin. If you want the 2015 version you can get one used on ebay.

Overall it’s a good doll for collectors, photographers, and artists.

If you're looking for a Made to Move doll with the same skin tone as the 1st Wave of Blue Top doll for a head swap, the blond Camping Fun- Rock Climber Barbie Made to Move is the perfect match.

text_fidelity_a:
Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game The predecessor to this game, Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective, is my all-time favorite game, and holds a high place on my game shelf despite being a “one and done” experience. Does this new iteration hold up to the high standard the previous game established?

To start with, the production value on this new version is heads and shoulders above the 2013 edition of SHCD that I own. The paper is printed on much nicer stock, the box is thicker and better designed to hold the contents, and the instruction manual in particular shows a great attention to detail that the previous edition lacked. I particularly like that in this edition, the solutions to each case are printed upside down in the back of the box, and that the solutions are encased in an envelope secured to each case book to prevent spoiling any aspects of the story with erroneous page turns.

Like the previous game, this “board game” is much more of a “choose your own adventure” story for you and your friends to solve. Each case is represented by a book, in which you’re given an introductory story, and then allowed free reign to investigate a variety of leads and allies to assist you in gathering information about whodunit. Once you think you know what’s happening, turn to the questions and find out what happened in this story – don’t worry, there are significant explanations and story to give closure to each case.

This is a stand-alone game, meaning that if you haven’t already played the original SHCD, you can purchase this with no strings attached. I don’t think I would recommend that for new players, however.

Jack the Ripper and the West End Adventures are quite different from what you get in the original game. In the original, there were some threads of story that remained from one case to the next, but in the new version, four of the cases are designed to be played campaign-style in an effort to solve the Jack the Ripper murders.

I’m sure that there will be many people out there who love the Jack the Ripper campaign - a set of four cases that are thematically tied together that will allow you to hunt down Jack using a separate map and additional investigative helpers – but it really isn’t for me. First of all, the cases are quite a bit darker and less whimsical than your traditional Sherlock Holmes story and case, and are tied together only by the fact that they occur in the same area and time period. I think the original cases are too difficult to be played by, let’s say, a 10 year old, but the stories wouldn’t be inappropriate for them in terms of language and description. The Jack cases, on the other hand, would carry a definite R-rating – they’re well-researched historically, and include lots of graphic description and a few cuss words as well. If you know anything about the historical Jack cases, you’d probably know this going in, but if you’re used to the style of the original cases, know that this is a darker affair. Secondly, you absolutely cannot find Jack and get a satisfactory conclusion until the fourth case, which is a decent investment in time with little return for parts 1 - 3. Third, and this is the big reason I didn’t like it, is that the mini-mysteries you’re solving in parts 1, 2 and 3 are not mysteries at all, but historical backstory. The questions are answered directly by particular sources, so if you visit the right allies and pursue the right leads you will simply be given the correct answers to each piece without putting much of anything together outside of remembering what the leads gave you. This was a very different experience, with a different writing style, different thematic elements, and a wholly different style, and since I am such a fan of the tried-and-true SHCD formula, I did not enjoy it as much as others may.

The other six cases are all stand-alone cases, and are quite good, although in most cases, they’re quite a bit harder than the already difficult cases in the original box. Like that set, some are better than others, but I will admit that the overall quality of these cases is on-par with what came in the original box, but still harder. I don’t think this is the right place to start with the SHCD universe.

Therein lies the only real problem that I have with this SHCD set – that while packaged as a stand-alone, this game is put together in a way that strongly suggests that it’s a sequel. If you think of it in movie terms, sure, you can watch most sequels without seeing the original movies, but why would you, especially if you know going in that watching the original is going to improve your experience? The cases in this box are more difficult, and the Jack the Ripper set is an odd starting place.

Overall, this game comes very highly recommended to any fan of the original set of cases. If this game sounds like something you’d be interested in, get it, but be advised that I think that the original set of 10 cases are a superior starting place.

4.5/5
text_fidelity_b: Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game

Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. Okay, so I got the kit and made the TWO potholders. I bought this kit because the loom was metal, and I'd read reviews and seen videos where the person's PLASTIC loom would break. So, what's the problem?
I really don't like how the loops slip off this loom, especially when you're getting towards completing the project. Pop, pop, pop go the loops - OFF the loom! This might be the nature of pot-holder looming, but I think the problem is the little spokes (hooks) are straight, so there's nothing to keep the loops from slipping off. They should be curved and WIDER at the top so the loops can't slide off. Towards the end, when you're crocheting the edges together, the last side can get completely unraveled.
THAT IS frustrating.
I'm going to try to find another loom.
Unfortunately, I looked at a lot looms before I bought this one, and they ALL seem to have the same design flaw.

Afterthought:
On a positive note: the loops are NOT polyester, but cotton, so the potholders came out nice 'n thick and heavy.
I can see why posters said they lasted a long time. They probably will.
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs.

Bezier Games Werebeasts Ted Alspach and his Bezier Games companies bring us another small-box Werewolf themed game. This game shares a similar deception element, and artwork with previous releases, but like "Werewords", this is not a mainline Werewolf game or expansion.

In this game, players are auctioning off beasts of various types, and players are bidding on these creatures, whether they truly want them or not. This is because one major mechanic of the game is calling other players out on collecting specific types of creatures - if you are correct that they are hoarding a specific creature-type, then they are punished

Ultimately, this game did not appeal to us. It has a learning curve to playing, but once you get the hang of it, it makes the game feel a little too random. No matter what you really want, you need to either make a large number of offers, or make remarkable guesses about which goals other players have. Both are legitimate ways to win, but like a more standard "classic" board game, there is a definite strategy that you want to use, and there isn't a lot of replayability in this one for our group.

In our group, the only player who really liked it was the winner, and even she wasn't entirely sold on this one. It's fast, and simple, but it's a little too easy to make guesses on what other players want, and the artwork is strange.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werebeasts

text_fidelity_a:
4DV5 Mini Drone for Kids with 720P Camera,FPV Live Video,LED Lights RC Quadcopter for Beginners,Boys and Girls Toys Gifts, Waypoints, Altitude Hold, Circle Fly,3D Flips,2 Battery,Orange First of all, my 9 year old son LOVED it! The LED lights are amazing and it was easy to watch in the dark at night, or just to enjoy during the day.

The "battery" is very different, you have to hook it up to the black device which has an USB and you need your own adapter to plug and recharge it. Each use lasts maybe 10 minutes max before you need to change batteries and recharge the first one. It is a great way to teach your child to take on different perspectives--if the drone is facing you, your left is actually its' right and your right is it's left. You have to consider that when using the controller just like with RC cars, except it is hard to tell from up in the air. You have to press left or right slightly to figure out which side then rotate it around so you can drive it. It comes with replacement spinners and a small screwdriver.

The return mode is nice, if you are freaking out and afraid it will go into a tree and unable to figure out which way to turn, just press that return button and it will come back to you.

Cons:
1. The drone was able to flip on the first day, but afterwards, for whatever reason, that stopped working. That didn't stop my son from enjoying it.
2. The video/camera app did not work on my phone. I tried different ways to get it to work.
3. Less than a week later, two of the "arms" that connect the ring to the base broke so now it won't lift up correctly. Even with superglue, that didn't help. Unfortunately, it is made of cheap flexible plastic.

So bottom line, I would not recommend buying this item.

This drone is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: 4DV5 Mini Drone for Kids with 720P Camera,FPV Live Video,LED Lights RC Quadcopter for Beginners,Boys and Girls Toys Gifts, Waypoints, Altitude Hold, Circle Fly,3D Flips,2 Battery,Orange

Craftabelle – Natural Charms Creation Kit – Bracelet Making Kit – 29pc Jewelry Set with Beads and Leather Cords – DIY Jewelry Kits for Kids Aged 8 Years + There IS a lead warning on the back of this box, so just want to be honest and open about that up front. The warning goes on to say however that the kit conforms to federal standards and is only a problem if eaten or chewed. You obviously don't want your kids to eat beads and stuff, and you may want to give this kit to a child who isn't bad about putting things in their mouth regardless.

That said, these kits are made for kids eight and up but honeslty, I think they should be marketed for any person 8 and up, since adults may like to try some of these crafts too. The kits are fun and easy to understand but may be complicated for some. The takeaway though is that the items available in this kit are available inexpensively a any craft store or large retailer and once you have completed the projects in the kit you can refill to keep making and designing them. These are a teaching tool after all but you can learn skills that you can use for years to come and these are all great. A little parental guidance for those who give to a preteen child and it will be OK. All the materials in this kit is decent quality.

text_fidelity_a:
The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games The Wolves is a quick game that looks easy to play, but it sure is not that.

The basic mechanic of the game is to manipulate your terrain tiles to perform actions, each of which can influence how fast the game accelerates, and how you manage to score points. Everything is controlled by these terrain tiles, and so you might choose a move actions specifically so that you can flip a tile that will allow you to use a Howl action. Or you may be lucky enough to flip three matches to Dominate an opponent's wolf, but that would require a lot of luck...or is it skill?

I would compare this game to 5 Tribes. None of the mechanics are similar in any way, but if you've played 5 Tribes, you might know that on your turn, you can likely identify ten different moves you could do, but it's mathematically impossible to always choose the correct action. In this game, you have a similar conundrum. What is the best move? Is it to howl at a wolf to put an extra marker on the board, or build a den that helps me establish area majority? There are turns where you legitimately have to decide between 5 different, equally powerful moves you can make, and then live with those consequences.

I do have one problem with the game, though, and that is that there are a lot of little rules to remember. Two pieces per space, you cannot be moved if you share a spot with a den, you have to re-move if someone "pushes" your pack wolves with an alpha, and alphas are the only ones who can howl. Dens can be upgraded to lairs if your den is next to water, but some spaces have rivers on them that look like water sources, but they aren't. Also, alphas have to be on the space to build a den, but can be adjacent to upgrade it. You get a reference card for some of this, and some is on the board, but it can be tricky to remember all of the specific placement rules for each different action.

This game is a lot thinkier than you might expect, and so it won't be for everyone. Everyone will want to play it though - the production quality of the game, from the art to the unique wolf meeples, is really quite excellent, and the game is rife with possibilities for expansions. The box insert is well-designed, and the maps are modular, which is great for replayability. Overall, our heavy gaming family liked our two plays of the game, and will come back to it often, because not too many games of this depth can be played this quickly.
text_fidelity_b: The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Werewords Deluxe Edition I very much liked the original edition of Werewords (essentially the same game as Insider), and this is the same game, but there's more of it.

Werewords is a lot like "20 questions". Players ask yes/no questions in an attempt to identify a word that could be anything from "spatula" to "Mjollnir". One player is a werewolf, who knows the word already, and is attempting to guide the players with their questioning closer to the actual word without them figuring out that they know the word already. They win if players can identify the word, but do not know which among them is the werewolf. If they do identify the werewolf, then the werewolf can also identify the "seer" player (another with information about the word).

The deluxe edition contains a few additional roles for players. If you already have the other version of this game, I don't think you need to own this version unless you're a completionist. If you don't own any versions of this game, I think it's quite good.

My concern remains the same as before - the app for this game is good, and it doesn't appear to be going anywhere, but if you don't want to run an app while playing this game, then I totally understand, and this game will not be for you at all. I think the app does a good job of balancing the words against one another, creating the ability to discern easy from very difficult words, but the same effect could have been accomplished with cards. I would prefer the cards as well, but the app has the advantage of saving shelf space and also having a larger directory of words. In the end, it's a toss up, but if you don't mind the app, then this is the best possible edition of the game to get.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werewords Deluxe Edition

text_fidelity_a:
Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor This is one of those toys that can provide HOURS of entertainment AND education. You're working those brain cells to build these railways! There's a booklet included with lots of different railways to build. It gives you step by step instructions by picture. You DO have to pay close attention to what color block you place where, and where the holes line up, and how many blocks you use. It all has to line up just right. That said, I wouldn't call this a difficult toy at all. It *will* exercise the mind, though.

I like using it with my 5 year old. It's helping him to follow directions. Of course, I still have to help a great deal. It's also helping him with counting, which he struggles with. It's helping my 2 year old learn his colors. Plus, we're ALL learning patience! ;) These railways fall down pretty easily, since it's basically stacking blocks on top of each other. Honestly, for most 2-3 year olds, I think this thing probably isn't the best idea just yet. For older children, it's wonderful. It has potential to grow with them for *years* to come. This is fun for adults, too! I've had a blast with it.

My ONLY complaint with this thing is the fact that the marbles have nothing to catch them as the come out of the final holes/blocks. They just roll away. We have a 7 month old that crawls everywhere and puts everything in his mouth. We're always careful, but playing with this thing, we have to be extraordinarily careful, especially due to the free rolling marble issue. So far, we haven't came up with a "catching place" for those last marbles, but I'm sure we will in time. We just can't use all the marbles at one time, and keep a close count on what we do use.

The extra caution we have to use is WELL worth it, though!!

This is the kind of toy you just can't go wrong with! (Unless you have children that might choke on those marbles...use your best judgment at that point). Highly recommended from us!
text_fidelity_b: Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor

Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min I'd never heard of Similo before, but there are other varieties of this card game(History and Myths...in June, at least). They can even be mixed with this one for a different game and there are instructions for doing so in this deck. The game is pretty simple. There's a Clue Giver and the other players are Guessers. The Clue Giver picks one of the characters in the deck(putting it back afterwards, along with 11 other cards) and then uses only cards leftover to give clues(5 cards in hand at a time), with no words or gestures. The 12 cards for the Guessers are spread in a grid and the Clue Giver gives one card per round for a clue. Vertical means there's something similar to the Secret Character and horizontal means there's something different. For example, if I'm the Clue Giver and I picked Aladdin, I could put Genie vertically, since they're from the same tale or I could put Cheshire Cat horizontally, since Aladdin isn't an animal. It's up the the Clue Giver to decide what's similar or different. The game is over within 5 rounds. The Guessers take away one card for the first round, two for the second, etc. If the Secret Character is taken away, the game is over, but if the final card is the Secret Character, the Guessers win.

I like that this game is cooperative. My children have to work together to win the game. We have plenty of competitive games, but very few cooperative ones, so this is a nice feature for us. I also like the illustrations on the cards. They're brightly colored and well done. It also doesn't take long to play, so if short on time, it's a nice way to pass just a bit of time and still have fun.
text_fidelity_b: Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min
